name: HVAC Air-Side (AHU / FCU / Ductwork / VAV) Installation, Balancing & Commissioning

activities: AHU plant-room slab / housekeeping plinths poured and cured
duct riser shaft openings and floor sleeves formed
fresh-air / exhaust louvre openings left in facade
structural support steel / Unistrut inserts and cast-in anchors set
plant-room walls and roof watertight (dry, weatherproofed space for AHU)
sequence.note: Air-side is enabled by civil, not built by it — foundations, plinths, wall openings and slab penetrations must precede any setting.

activities: AHU / large FCU delivered, rigged and set on vibration isolators / plinth
roof or plant-room access and lifting path confirmed for the AHU footprint
unit anchored, level checked, drain pan positioned
sequence.note: AHUs are set early because they are large and drive the duct main routing; heavy lift must precede surrounding trades closing the space.

activities: duct hangers, brackets, trapeze supports and seismic restraints installed to layout
riser supports and floor penetration frames fixed
sequence.note: Supports precede duct erection; hanging duct off finished supports, not vice-versa.

activities: main duct runs, risers and branch ductwork erected and joined
VAV / terminal boxes hung and connected into supply mains
FCUs hung and connected to supply/return duct or plenum
fire/smoke dampers set in rated wall/floor penetrations
flexible connections to fans/AHU fitted
sequence.note: Erect mains first, then branches, then terminal units; fire dampers coordinated with rated-barrier construction.

activities: volume control dampers, access doors, turning vanes fitted
diffusers, grilles and registers set (often after ceiling grid)
duct-mounted sensors, actuators and control dampers mounted
sequence.note: Terminal grilles/diffusers usually follow ceiling installation; interface with architectural ceilings.

activities: ductwork sectionalised and leakage (pressure) tested per class before concealment
witnessed leakage test on high-pressure supply mains
sequence.note: Leakage test MUST occur before ceilings close and before insulation covers seams.

activities: thermal/acoustic duct insulation applied
vapour barrier and cladding on external / plant-room duct
sequence.note: Insulation follows a passed leakage test — never insulate an untested seam.

activities: AHU / FCU / VAV power feeds terminated
control wiring to actuators, sensors, VFDs landed
VFD / starter connected and meggered
sequence.note: Requires containment + cable pulling complete; feeds from the electrical system must be live-ready.

activities: fan rotation / direction check, bearing and belt check
static leak and damper stroke checks
filter installation, coil clean
point-to-point control I/O verification with BMS
sequence.note: Motor solo-run and control point checks precede any air movement for balancing.

activities: Testing, Adjusting & Balancing (TAB): measure and set supply/return/exhaust airflow at every terminal
set fan speed / VFD reference, adjust volume dampers and VAV min/max
record airflow, static pressure, fan curve, sound where specified
sequence.note: TAB requires the FULL air path complete and stable: all ceilings/diffusers in, filters clean, BMS driving dampers; a partial system cannot be balanced.

activities: integrated functional test with BMS: occupancy, setpoint, economizer, night setback
smoke/fire damper trip and fan interlock test with fire alarm
cause-and-effect / integrated systems test
performance verification against design airflow and temperature
sequence.note: Final commissioning integrates the chilled-water side, BMS and fire alarm; it is the last stage and depends on every upstream system being live.

typical_relationships.before: AHU plant-room plinth / slab poured and cured
typical_relationships.reason: The unit cannot be placed and levelled until its foundation plinth exists and has gained strength.
Ductwork is hung from supports; erecting duct before its supports are fixed is not physically possible.
Branches and terminal units tap off the main; the trunk defines routing and must exist first.
Insulation conceals joints; testing after insulating means tearing off insulation to find leaks.

typical_relationships.after: Ceiling / drywall closure over the duct route
typical_relationships.reason: Concealed duct must be proven leak-tight before it is covered by ceilings.
Terminal air devices are supported by and coordinated with the finished ceiling.

typical_relationships.before: Fire/smoke damper installed and rated barrier built
typical_relationships.reason: Dampers must be set within the rated wall/floor before the penetration is sealed and inspected.

typical_relationships.before: AHU/fan power and control wiring terminated
typical_relationships.reason: A motor cannot be energised for direction check until its feeder and controls are landed and meggered.

typical_relationships.before: All diffusers, dampers and filters installed; BMS driving the system
typical_relationships.reason: Airflow can only be measured and set on a complete, stable air path — a partial system gives meaningless readings.
Functional performance and control sequences are verified against balanced design airflows, so balancing must finish first.
Running a fan without filters fouls coils and gives false static-pressure and airflow readings.

typical_relationships.before: Chilled-water coil connected and CHW available
typical_relationships.reason: Supply-air temperature and coil capacity can only be verified once cooling medium is flowing.

interfaces.requirement: AHU plinths, plant-room slab, duct riser shaft openings, facade louvre openings and cast-in support anchors must be complete before AHU setting and duct erection.
Support steel, inserts and trapeze anchorage for duct mains and risers must be available before ductwork is hung.

AHU/FCU cooling coils require CHW piping connected, flushed and flow available before air-side temperature performance can be commissioned; air balancing (TAB) is typically coordinated with water balancing.
AHU/fan/VAV motors and VFDs require permanent (or commissioning) power feeds terminated and energised before solo run and balancing.
Power and control cabling to units requires cable tray/containment installed and cables pulled and terminated first.
VAV/damper/actuator/sensor control points must be wired to and verified by the BMS (point-to-point) so the BMS can drive dampers during balancing and functional commissioning.
Fire/smoke dampers and fan shutdown interlocks require fire-alarm cause-and-effect live to test damper trip and fan stop.
Duct/space temperature, pressure and airflow sensors must be installed and calibrated before control loops and balancing can be validated.
Thermal/acoustic duct insulation is applied only after the duct leakage test passes; insulation must not precede testing.
Ceiling-void congestion is shared with sprinkler mains; duct routing and support must be coordinated with fire-fighting pipe to avoid clashes.

testing_requirements: Ductwork air-leakage (pressure) test to specified duct pressure class, witnessed, before concealment and insulation
Fan/motor insulation resistance (megger) test before energisation
Fan rotation / direction and vibration check on solo run
Damper and actuator stroke / end-position verification
BMS point-to-point (I/O) verification for all air-side sensors, actuators and VFDs
Testing, Adjusting & Balancing (TAB) report: measured vs design airflow at every terminal, fan static, VFD reference
Fire/smoke damper trip test and fan-shutdown interlock with fire alarm
Filter installation verification and coil cleanliness check
Integrated functional / cause-and-effect test of control sequences (economizer, setpoint, night setback)
Sound-level and space-condition (temperature/humidity) performance verification where specified
commissioning_dependencies: Permanent (or temporary commissioning) power energised to all fans/AHUs/VFDs
Chilled water available, flushed and balanced to the cooling coils
BMS live with verified control points driving dampers, VFDs and valves
Fire alarm cause-and-effect live for damper/fan interlocks
All terminal devices (diffusers/grilles/dampers) installed and ceilings closed so the air path is complete
Filters installed, coils clean, access doors sealed
Duct leakage test passed on all concealed sections
TAB (air balancing) completed and accepted before integrated performance testing

work_packages.note: interfaces with passive fire and fire alarm
interfaces with chilled_water balancing and bms

typical_exceptions: Small split/DX FCU packages may skip duct leakage testing where there is little or no ductwork.
Roof-mounted package units combine AHU setting and E&I on a factory skid, collapsing the setting and rough-in stages.
In fast-track fit-outs diffusers are sometimes set into an open ceiling before final grid, reversing the usual ceiling-first order.
Constant-volume systems have no VAV boxes, so terminal-box connection stages do not apply.
Displacement/plenum-return designs have no return ductwork, so return-side erection and balancing are reduced.
evidence: Air balancing (TAB) is scheduled before, or without, the full air path being complete — no diffusers/ceilings in place, filters missing, or the BMS not yet driving dampers — so the balanced airflows cannot be valid; likewise duct insulation or ceiling closure precedes the witnessed duct leakage test.
